description.narrative: The project is implemented in Zimbabwe. The main target groups are women and men in five community based organisations (CBOs) that Media Institute of Southern Africa-Zimbabwe Chapter (MISA Zimbabwe) will work with across sectors, including womens groups, resident associations, farming communities and youth. Through training, information dissemination social media and community outreach the project aims to achieve citizens that enjoy their constitutional guaranteed rights to access information and hold public officials accountable.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Media Institute of Southern Africa-Zimbabwe Chapter (MISA Zimbabwe) and the Palme Center. MISA-Zimbabwe has over the years been the leading advocate for media freedom, freedom of expression and access to information and has drafted alternative laws, fact sheets and position papers, which have been used as reference points by some government ministries in their media policy formulation. Also, these model laws have been adopted as lobby tools by the umbrella alliance body, the Media Alliance of Zimbabwe.Other Donors to the OrganisationThe organisation receives both institutional and programme support from SIDA, HIVOS and IMS.Project ObjectiveInfluencing policy makers to adopt democratic policies and leveraging available alternative communication platforms to promote freedom of expression and access to information. Against this backdrop, the envisaged Outcomes of the proposed project are as follows: Policy makers and key actors engaged to adopt democratic legislative framework and practice that promotes freedom of expression and access to information through free communication platforms. Targeted communities mobilised to demand information and use it to hold leadership to account. Targeted communities access relevant information and news through leveraging alternative platforms. Strengthened MISA Zimbabwe through continuous development of its systems, structures and offices and mainstreaming gender it its policies and interventions. To promote access to the internet in selected Zimbabwean communities and capacitate targeted community activists, citizen journalists, youths with skills and tools to circumvent online information controlsActor groupsJournalists, decision-makers at various platforms, parliament portfolio committees, community-based organisations and activists.
